clippings.speaker: Ingmar Bergman
clippings.quote: Sometimes I probably do mourn the fact that I no longer make films… Most of all I miss working with Sven Nykvist, perhaps because we are both utterly captivated by the problems of light, the gentle, dangerous, dreamlike, living, dead, clear, misty, hot, violent, bare, sudden, dark, springlike, falling, straight, slanting, sensual, subdue, limited, poisonous, calming, pale light. Light.
clippings.title: Sven Nykvist, cinematographer, master of light
clippings.context: Nykvist's obituary quoting Bergman's autobiography The Magic Lantern (translated from Swedish), written after he stopped making films.

clippings.speaker: Ingmar Bergman
clippings.quote: The only thing that I miss with not making films anymore is that I don’t get to work with Sven.
clippings.title: Nykvist was 'the master of light'
clippings.context: Variety's obituary quoting what Bergman said in Carl-Gustaf Nykvist's documentary Light Keeps Me Company.

clippings.speaker: Ingmar Bergman
clippings.quote: Sven and I saw things alike, thought things alike; our feeling for light was the same. We had the same basic moral positions about camera placement.
clippings.title: Sven Nykvist - Writer
clippings.context: Reference entry (Patricia Ferrara, updated by Rob Edelman) quoting Bergman in the documentary Light Keeps Me Company.

clippings.speaker: Sven Nykvist
clippings.quote: I was fortunate to work with Ingmar, especially at that early stage in my career. One of the things we believed was that a picture shouldn’t look lit. Whenever possible, I lit with one source and avoided creating shadows, because that pointed to the photography.
clippings.title: Beyond The Frame: Cries and Whispers
clippings.context: Nykvist speaking to American Cinematographer (AP dates the remark to 1995), resurfaced in the ASC's Beyond the Frame series.

clippings.speaker: Sven Nykvist
clippings.quote: That was a very nice way to work… Everyone did everything. Everyone helped everyone else. it was like a family. Even Cries and Whispers was produced on a $300,000 to $400,000 budget. I learned so much about composition, staging and the infinite varieties of light from Ingmar.
clippings.title: Beyond The Frame: Cries and Whispers
clippings.context: Nykvist on Bergman's tiny crews and budgets, from the same American Cinematographer interview.

clippings.speaker: Sven Nykvist
clippings.quote: Initially, I was quite apprehensive; Ingmar was known as the ‘demonic’ director. But from the first day, we worked well together. Perhaps we understood each other because we were both the sons of pastors.
clippings.title: Sven Nykvist interview from Cinematography Screencraft by Peter Ettedgui
clippings.context: Nykvist's first-person account in Peter Ettedgui's book, reproduced on a blog in 2010, on first meeting Bergman.

clippings.speaker: Sven Nykvist
clippings.quote: The next day, when we saw the rushes, Ingmar screamed, “God Damn it! How can there be shadows when the sun has gone down?” The incident marked the beginning of our journey together into light… Had I not met him, in all probability I would have remained just another technician with no great awareness of the infinite possibilities of light.
clippings.title: Sven Nykvist interview from Cinematography Screencraft by Peter Ettedgui
clippings.context: Nykvist recalling adding artificial light to a night exterior on The Virgin Spring, his second film for Bergman.

notes: All three Bergman quotes are secondhand (memoir/documentary as quoted in obituaries/reference); the Ettedgui book excerpt is read on a blog reprint, not the publisher. ascmag.com blocked.
